voice.refText: You wake up and discover you can pause time. 10 seconds once a day. At first, you use it for dumb things. You catch your falling coffee. You dodge your boss in the hallway.

Mother.describe: A warm, low female alto: a mother in her late fifties in her own kitchen. Unhurried and teasing, soft-spoken, a little husky, a light Filipino English lilt, love under every plain word.

Aunt one.describe: A sweet, chirpy female voice, a high mezzo: an aunt in her sixties. Fond and a little vague, delighted with her phone, a light Filipino English lilt.

Aunt two.describe: A grand, slow female alto: an aunt in her sixties. Gracious and dramatic, savouring every word, a light Filipino English lilt.

Bus kid.describe: A high, bright boy's voice, about eight years old. Curious and earnest, whispering loudly on a night bus.

Shift lead.describe: A soft, low female voice, an alto: a call-centre shift lead in her forties at two in the morning. A hushed whisper, firm and kind, used to keeping a room quiet.

Best friend.describe: A bright, tired female mezzo: a woman of about thirty who works night shifts at a call centre. Quick and warm, a laugh close under the words, hoarse at the edges from talking all night, casual modern English.

Coworker.describe: A soft, low female voice, an alto: a call-centre worker in her twenties at four in the morning. A hushed whisper, protective and tired.

Manager.describe: A smooth, clipped male baritone: an office boss in his forties in a tie. Confident and transactional, quietly pleased with himself, every sentence a deal.

Cousin.describe: A bright, sunny female soprano: a cousin in her twenties working abroad, waving into a phone camera. Cheerful and a little homesick, a light Filipino English lilt.

Newsreader.describe: A polished male baritone: a television newsreader in his fifties. Measured and authoritative, crisp diction, a calm studio cadence.

lines.text: Mother: Make a wish. A real one.
lines.say: [warm, teasing, shielding a candle] Make a wish. A real one.
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: Mother: What? What is it?
lines.say: [alarmed, leaning in, half a laugh] What? What is it?
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: You asked who meant it. The candle gave you something better.
lines.say: [sly, delighted, a secret shared] You asked who meant it. The candle gave you something better.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So what if you could see who uses AI to text you? Everyone who did. Every time.
lines.say: [quick, conspiratorial, the last four words savoured] So what if you could see who uses AI to text you? Everyone who did. Every time.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Catch anyone you like. Just never get caught catching.
lines.say: [sly, quick, a dare, a grin on the last word] Catch anyone you like. Just never get caught catching.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Forty-one birthday wishes. Thirty-three dots. One on your best friend's paragraph. Even her.
lines.say: [brisk, amazed, a gasp of a laugh on the last two words] Forty-one birthday wishes. Thirty-three dots. One on your best friend's paragraph. Even her.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And the only wish you'd have marked down for spelling is the only one a person typed. Your father. Eight months out on a cargo ship. Three words, one wrong. Same as always.
lines.say: [dry, amused, fond on the last three words] And the only wish you'd have marked down for spelling is the only one a person typed. Your father. Eight months out on a cargo ship. Three words, one wrong. Same as always.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You've always graded people by their messages. Long means love. Short means busy. A typo means they couldn't be bothered.
lines.say: [teasing, quick, a confession on your behalf] You've always graded people by their messages. Long means love. Short means busy. A typo means they couldn't be bothered.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The rule. Every message you can read, in any app, from anyone, a text, a comment, a review: if a machine chose the words, it gets a small red dot. Whoever's thumbs pressed send.
lines.say: [clear, brisk, exact, each item a beat, the last sentence pointed] The rule. Every message you can read, in any app, from anyone, a text, a comment, a review: if a machine chose the words, it gets a small red dot. Whoever's thumbs pressed send.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Only you see them. They are never wrong.
lines.say: [plain, certain, a little thrilled] Only you see them. They are never wrong.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But a dot says who wrote it. It never says why. Remember that.
lines.say: [measured, slower, the last two words almost a whisper] But a dot says who wrote it. It never says why. Remember that.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mother: Dots? What dots?
lines.say: [puzzled, holding the phone to the window, mild] Dots? What dots?
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: Your father is one of about two million Filipinos working overseas. For a family like yours, the phone is where home is.
lines.say: [steady, warm, the fact said plainly] Your father is one of about two million Filipinos working overseas. For a family like yours, the phone is where home is.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Four words in, and your own phone offers to be you. In grey.
lines.say: [quick, amused, then cool on the last two words] Four words in, and your own phone offers to be you. In grey.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You don't send it. First: who else?
lines.say: [sly, a plan forming, a hook on the last two words] You don't send it. First: who else?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You go through your phone like customs.
lines.say: [brisk, amused, officious] You go through your phone like customs.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your boss. So proud of this team, a whole paragraph. Dot. Your sick day, noted. No dot. He only types the bad news.
lines.say: [dry, a wince of a joke on the last sentence] Your boss. So proud of this team, a whole paragraph. Dot. Your sick day, noted. No dot. He only types the bad news.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your two aunts. Eleven messages this week, all between them.
lines.say: [amused, setting up a trick] Your two aunts. Eleven messages this week, all between them.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Aunt one: Lovely.
lines.say: [pleased, reading her one word aloud as she types it] Lovely.
lines.speaker: Aunt one

lines.text: Aunt two: She writes so beautifully.
lines.say: [proud, moved, to nobody] She writes so beautifully.
lines.speaker: Aunt two

lines.text: Aunt one: Forgive me? For what?
lines.say: [baffled, indignant, to the phone] Forgive me? For what?
lines.speaker: Aunt one

lines.text: Nobody did anything. Two machines fought and made up all week, and both aunts are proud of them.
lines.say: [deadpan, a laugh held under it] Nobody did anything. Two machines fought and made up all week, and both aunts are proud of them.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Now, the obvious move. Why not just ask?
lines.say: [conspiratorial, the comment section's voice] Now, the obvious move. Why not just ask?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Aunt one: Every word, my love.
lines.say: [sweet, sincere, beaming] Every word, my love.
lines.speaker: Aunt one

lines.text: Dot. On the answer. You can't just ask. People lie. Dots don't.
lines.say: [a beat of silence first, then quick and gleeful, the last four words clipped] Dot. On the answer. You can't just ask. People lie. Dots don't.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your mother's eat first, every letter fixed by the phone. Bare. Chosen words get a dot. Fixed letters don't.
lines.say: [fond, then exact, a rule being learned] Your mother's eat first, every letter fixed by the phone. Bare. Chosen words get a dot. Fixed letters don't.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Nobody suspects a thing. In a study of more than 1,300 Americans, people read a personal message. Told it was written by AI, they called the sender lazy and insincere. Told nothing, most never suspected.
lines.say: [hushed, a secret, the fact quick and clear, a grin on the last sentence] Nobody suspects a thing. In a study of more than thirteen hundred Americans, people read a personal message. Told it was written by AI, they called the sender lazy and insincere. Told nothing, most never suspected.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But here's problem one. You've checked everyone except the one you're afraid to.
lines.say: [leaning in, low, the last word soft] But here's problem one. You've checked everyone except the one you're afraid to.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your best friend. Bea. Eleven years. Her paragraph had a dot on it.
lines.say: [quieter, careful, a detective naming a suspect] Your best friend. Bea. Eleven years. Her paragraph had a dot on it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You don't ask. You know what asking gets you. You test. The one thing no machine could know.
lines.say: [quick, cunning, pleased with yourself] You don't ask. You know what asking gets you. You test. The one thing no machine could know.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Perfect. In nine seconds. Dot.
lines.say: [stunned, then flat on the last word] Perfect. In nine seconds. Dot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So the machine knows about the goat. Which means somewhere, there's a file on you.
lines.say: [slow, thrilled and a little spooked, the last five words a whisper] So the machine knows about the goat. Which means somewhere, there's a file on you.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You delete your long reply. Two letters.
lines.say: [clipped, cold, decisive] You delete your long reply. Two letters.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Two seconds. Dot. Then you make the mistake every detective makes. You check your own pockets.
lines.say: [dry, quick, a hook on the last sentence] Two seconds. Dot. Then you make the mistake every detective makes. You check your own pockets.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your sent folder. A year back.
lines.say: [hushed, a held breath, a dare] Your sent folder. A year back.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your thank-you to your boss. Dot. Half this morning's thank-yous. Dots. You've been grading people for a crime you commit before breakfast.
lines.say: [each dot a small blow, then a laugh at yourself on the last sentence] Your thank-you to your boss. Dot. Half this morning's thank-yous. Dots. You've been grading people for a crime you commit before breakfast.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: For years, Gmail has offered to suggest your replies and finish your sentences as you type.
lines.say: [calm, exact, a fact that lands on you] For years, Gmail has offered to suggest your replies and finish your sentences as you type.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The detective is a suspect.
lines.say: [deadpan, a complete thought] The detective is a suspect.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You typed that a year ago, after a fight with her, and forgot. The machine didn't.
lines.say: [quick, a little amazed, the last three words slow] You typed that a year ago, after a fight with her, and forgot. The machine didn't.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You switch every suggestion off. Not guilt. Strategy. You can't see everyone's dots and be covered in them.
lines.say: [brisk, hard, a plan] You switch every suggestion off. Not guilt. Strategy. You can't see everyone's dots and be covered in them.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Problem two. Now you think dots predict people. So you bet dinner on them.
lines.say: [leaning in, sly, a turn on the last sentence] Problem two. Now you think dots predict people. So you bet dinner on them.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Saturday. Your mother's party for you. Twenty wouldn't-miss-its. You count the dots. Nineteen.
lines.say: [quick, amused, counting] Saturday. Your mother's party for you. Twenty wouldn't-miss-its. You count the dots. Nineteen.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mother: Twenty said yes.
lines.say: Twenty said yes.
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: One came. Not your cousin, the bare yes: she only calls in from abroad. Your best friend, dotted all week, in your kitchen anyway.
lines.say: [deadpan, then a small puzzled note on the last five words] One came. Not your cousin, the bare yes: she only calls in from abroad. Your best friend, dotted all week, in your kitchen anyway.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mother: Twenty said yes.
lines.say: [firm, proud, a spoon in hand] Twenty said yes.
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: Your mother sends your father a photo of nineteen clean plates. His reply, in seconds.
lines.say: [dry, setting up] Your mother sends your father a photo of nineteen clean plates. His reply, in seconds.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: No dot. You don't call. You're busy predicting the future. As long as the future is a dinner party.
lines.say: [quick, self-mocking, a grin] No dot. You don't call. You're busy predicting the future. As long as the future is a dinner party.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But your best friend's dot still doesn't fit. Two seconds, every time, at four in the morning. You go and catch her at it.
lines.say: [low, nosy, a detective on a stakeout] But your best friend's dot still doesn't fit. Two seconds, every time, at four in the morning. You go and catch her at it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Two a.m. The night bus.
lines.say: [hushed, quick, a city going by] Two a.m. The night bus.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Bus kid: How do you spell sorry?
lines.say: [small, serious, tongue out, six years old] How do you spell sorry?
lines.speaker: Bus kid

lines.text: Six years old. Not a dot on him.
lines.say: [dry, approving, a little envious] Six years old. Not a dot on him.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Shift lead: Twelve hours. Don't wake her.
lines.say: [whispered, firm, kind] Twelve hours. Don't wake her.
lines.speaker: Shift lead

lines.text: That's who answers you at four in the morning. Her, a year ago, making sure she'd never miss you.
lines.say: [quiet, the one soft line, a small smile in it] That's who answers you at four in the morning. Her, a year ago, making sure she'd never miss you.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: A dot never says why. That's a why.
lines.say: [low, plain, the plant paying off] A dot never says why. That's a why.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Best friend: You came?
lines.say: [half asleep, hoarse, glad] You came?
lines.speaker: Best friend

lines.text: Best friend: Eleven years, and you sent me ok.
lines.say: [a laugh breaking in it, not angry, awake now] Eleven years, and you sent me ok.
lines.speaker: Best friend

lines.text: Her machine is still texting you while she's talking to you. You'd have bet the house on that dot.
lines.say: [quick, delighted, a laugh under the second sentence] Her machine is still texting you while she's talking to you. You'd have bet the house on that dot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Monday. The office. The client complains. Your coworker takes it.
lines.say: [brisk, a scene set in four strokes] Monday. The office. The client complains. Your coworker takes it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Coworker: Ten minutes. I'll write something.
lines.say: [breezy, confident, already typing] Ten minutes. I'll write something.
lines.speaker: Coworker

lines.text: He writes something. Dot.
lines.say: [deadpan, a beat before the last word] He writes something. Dot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Coworker: Prove it.
lines.say: [cocky, arms folded] Prove it.
lines.speaker: Coworker

lines.text: You can't. A screenshot comes out clean. Nobody else sees a dot.
lines.say: [flat, a little stung, exact] You can't. A screenshot comes out clean. Nobody else sees a dot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Coworker: Fine. I'll type it myself.
lines.say: [huffy, defiant] Fine. I'll type it myself.
lines.speaker: Coworker

lines.text: Coworker: I typed every letter!
lines.say: [outraged, betrayed by his own thumbs] I typed every letter!
lines.speaker: Coworker

lines.text: Dot. The dot follows who chose the words, not whose thumbs moved.
lines.say: [gleeful, exact, the rule recited like a verdict] Dot. The dot follows who chose the words, not whose thumbs moved.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So you prove it the one way you can. Out loud. Right, three times in a row.
lines.say: [quick, building, a showman] So you prove it the one way you can. Out loud. Right, three times in a row.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: By lunch, the whole floor types with its thumbs. Like an exam.
lines.say: [dry, delighted, hushed on the last three words] By lunch, the whole floor types with its thumbs. Like an exam.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Manager: How do you know?
lines.say: [quiet, curious, a pen already moving] How do you know?
lines.speaker: Manager

lines.text: You shrug. He writes that down. By hand. Trouble is, everybody wants to plug in the lie detector.
lines.say: [amused, then a shade of warning on the last sentence] You shrug. He writes that down. By hand. Trouble is, everybody wants to plug in the lie detector.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then you look up, and the city is red.
lines.say: [wide, a breath of awe, a grin] Then you look up, and the city is red.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The restaurant downstairs. Five stars, dotted, every one. One bare review: two stars, fish was ok, waiter was rude. You eat there.
lines.say: [brisk, amused, the review read flat, a decision on the last three words] The restaurant downstairs. Five stars, dotted, every one. One bare review: two stars, fish was ok, waiter was rude. You eat there.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: One bare review. First useful thing you've read all day.
lines.say: [deadpan, pleased, a verdict] One bare review. First useful thing you've read all day.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Cousin: Thank you all so much. I love you all.
lines.say: [bright, tearful, waving at a camera] Thank you all so much. I love you all.
lines.speaker: Cousin

lines.text: Four hundred comments under your cousin's video. A field of red. She's crying at bots.
lines.say: [wry, then a laugh on the last sentence] Four hundred comments under your cousin's video. A field of red. She's crying at bots.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The dating-app man. A month of flirting, never typed a word. He asks you to dinner. Dotted.
lines.say: [dry, quick, the last word flat] The dating-app man. A month of flirting, never typed a word. He asks you to dinner. Dotted.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: His first real message. Bare. Awful. You say yes.
lines.say: [deadpan, a grin on the last three words] His first real message. Bare. Awful. You say yes.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You can make one man type. You can't make a city do it. And now the people in charge find out.
lines.say: [quick, wry, then a chill on the last sentence] You can make one man type. You can't make a city do it. And now the people in charge find out.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Newsreader: The senator's apology has now been shared over a million times.
lines.say: [measured, professional, a newsroom cadence] The senator's apology has now been shared over a million times.
lines.speaker: Newsreader

lines.text: Dot. A machine apologised, a million machines accepted, and your mother cried.
lines.say: [deadpan, quick, a laugh on the last four words] Dot. A machine apologised, a million machines accepted, and your mother cried.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mother: He sounds so sincere.
lines.say: [moved, a hand to her chest] He sounds so sincere.
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: You could call the station. And say what?
lines.say: [dry, a shrug in the voice] You could call the station. And say what?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then your boss. The senator's rival wants a list of which supporters are real. A bonus bigger than a year's pay. It arrives with a dot. He didn't even write it.
lines.say: [low, tempted, then flat and amused on the last two sentences] Then your boss. The senator's rival wants a list of which supporters are real. A bonus bigger than a year's pay. It arrives with a dot. He didn't even write it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: That bonus could bring your father home for good.
lines.say: [low, tempted, quiet] That bonus could bring your father home for good.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You'd sell. Everyone would. But a dot never says why. Half of those dotted supporters are tired people who let a phone finish a sentence. If a machine wrote it but they meant it, does it still count? The first one who proves she's real, you're the fraud, and every liar in town has your name. Keep it, and it stays yours.
lines.say: [quick, both sides weighed, the question put straight to you, dread on the fraud, hard and certain on the last sentence] You'd sell. Everyone would. But a dot never says why. Half of those dotted supporters are tired people who let a phone finish a sentence. If a machine wrote it but they meant it, does it still count? The first one who proves she's real, you're the fraud, and every liar in town has your name. Keep it, and it stays yours.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So you do the cleverest thing all week. You hand him everything.
lines.say: [sly, relishing it, a pause before the last sentence] So you do the cleverest thing all week. You hand him everything.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Manager: There's nothing there.
lines.say: [flat, puzzled, handing it back] There's nothing there.
lines.speaker: Manager

lines.text: Nobody can buy what nobody can see. The flaw in the power is the lock on it.
lines.say: [triumphant, quiet, a complete thought] Nobody can buy what nobody can see. The flaw in the power is the lock on it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: On the roof, you see what keeping them buys. Try not to enjoy it.
lines.say: [wide, then a grin on the last sentence] On the roof, you see what keeping them buys. Try not to enjoy it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Around the turn of the century, the Philippines was called the texting capital of the world. Every lit window is a chat. From up here, you see the dots.
lines.say: [awe, slow, hushed on the last sentence] Around the turn of the century, the Philippines was called the texting capital of the world. Every lit window is a chat. From up here, you see the dots.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Now take away the dotted ones.
lines.say: [very quiet, a dare, a smile in it] Now take away the dotted ones.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Half the city is talking, and nobody's home. And you're the only person alive who knows which half.
lines.say: [awe, slow, then a thrill on the last sentence] Half the city is talking, and nobody's home. And you're the only person alive who knows which half.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your phone buzzes on the roof. A calendar reminder you never set.
lines.say: [puzzled, quick, a hook] Your phone buzzes on the roof. A calendar reminder you never set.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You delete it. At nine, you go anyway.
lines.say: [dry, then a decision, amused at yourself] You delete it. At nine, you go anyway.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Best friend: You booked this?
lines.say: [surprised, wary, hopeful] You booked this?
lines.speaker: Best friend

lines.text: Best friend: ...Neither did I.
lines.say: [slow, a dawning, almost a laugh] Neither did I.
lines.speaker: Best friend

lines.text: Two phones. The night you made up, three months ago. Every line. Both sides. Dotted.
lines.say: [quick, then each of the last five words alone, amazed] Two phones. The night you made up, three months ago. Every line. Both sides. Dotted.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Her instruction. Yours. Two machines, told the same thing by two people who were asleep, made up on your behalf and booked you a cafe.
lines.say: [wonder, a laugh starting under it, building to the last five words] Her instruction. Yours. Two machines, told the same thing by two people who were asleep, made up on your behalf and booked you a cafe.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In a 2023 study, people who suspected their chat partner was using AI-suggested replies judged them more harshly. Using them made the conversation warmer and closer.
lines.say: [calm, exact, the second sentence plain and a little pleased] In a twenty twenty-three study, people who suspected their chat partner was using AI-suggested replies judged them more harshly. Using them made the conversation warmer and closer.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Neither of you wrote it. Both of you still came. Phones face down. Nothing to dot. Now you have to talk. Harder than it looks.
lines.say: [warm, quick, a laugh on the last sentence] Neither of you wrote it. Both of you still came. Phones face down. Nothing to dot. Now you have to talk. Harder than it looks.

lines.text: That evening. Your boss. No dot.
lines.say: [quiet, a chill, each fragment alone] That evening. Your boss. No dot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The first thing he's ever typed to you himself. You taught him what bare looks like. Not why he sent it.
lines.say: [low, dread with a dry laugh in it, the last sentence pointed] The first thing he's ever typed to you himself. You taught him what bare looks like. Not why he sent it.

lines.text: Your father, still at the bottom. Three words, one wrong. Send. No dot. Obviously.
lines.say: [brisk, fond, a shrug on the last word] Your father, still at the bottom. Three words, one wrong. Send. No dot. Obviously.

lines.text: Mother: He never could spell.
lines.say: [fond, not turning round, a smile in it] He never could spell.

lines.text: Then your cousin drops a voice note. The first voice in a chat that's only ever been text.
lines.say: [quick, curious, a hook held back] Then your cousin drops a voice note. The first voice in a chat that's only ever been text.

lines.text: So, how many of your last ten texts would get a dot? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
lines.say: [direct, sly, a grin] So, how many of your last ten texts would get a dot? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
